questions.q: What is the key difference between naming a steward role and running a stewardship program?
options: The program is the operational machinery — recruiting, time allocation, support, tracking — that makes the role actually function across domains
There is no difference; they mean the same thing
A stewardship program only applies to IT staff, while the role applies to everyone
The role is temporary while the program is permanent by law
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes a role definition (Foundations Lesson 14) from the operational program that makes that role function in practice.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say steward recruitment is really a negotiation with the steward's manager?
options: Stewards almost always already have an existing job, so their time has to be explicitly carved out and protected
Managers are legally required to approve all data roles
Stewards are typically brand-new hires with no existing manager
The program has no authority to select stewards without HR involvement
questions.explain: Because stewardship is added on top of an existing job, the manager must agree the allocated time is real and protected.

questions.q: What time allocation range does the lesson mention as common for stewardship work?
options: Roughly 10-20% of the steward's week
100% of their week, as a full-time role
Exactly one hour per year
Whatever time is left over with no stated percentage
questions.explain: The lesson specifically calls for an explicit, written allocation, commonly in the 10-20% range, rather than leaving it undefined.

questions.q: What does a steward community of practice provide?
options: A recurring peer forum where stewards across domains share solutions and build consistency
A formal legal body that approves governance policy
A replacement for the governance council
A one-time training session with no ongoing meetings
questions.explain: The community of practice is described as an ongoing, informal peer forum — distinct from the formal council/committee structure.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what should happen when tracking shows a steward's negotiated time allocation no longer matches their real workload?
options: The program should add stewards or formally increase allocated time, not expect the steward to just absorb it
The steward should be replaced immediately
The data quality issues should be closed without resolution
Nothing — workload mismatches are expected and require no action
questions.explain: The lesson frames a workload mismatch as a signal for the program (and often the sponsor) to act, not something stewards should silently absorb.
